chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the purchase of a slave from the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma) when they acknowledge/consent to that for them. He said: 'When they acknowledge/consent to that for them, then buy and marry.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ اَلذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying slaves from the People of the Covenant according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the validity of purchasing slaves from the Ahl al-Dhimma, contingent upon their explicit consent. The Imam’s concise ruling not only validates the commercial transaction but also extends permission to marry these slaves, reflecting the practical application of manumission and integration within the early Shia jurisprudential framework.
